# Results — Study 844 (Madden-Cover-Curse)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"Buy the hype into the new Madden / NBA 2K"**: does the publisher (EA for *Madden*, TTWO
for *NBA 2K*) earn an abnormal return running into, and coming out of, the annual game
launch? Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

*Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month).
Fingerprint `a8dd4e62fc5d` (EA + TTWO + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `EA` (Electronic Arts) + `TTWO` (Take-Two) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 3,038 rows, 2014-06-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 20 annual launches — 10 *Madden NFL* (Madden 16→25, EA) + 10 *NBA 2K* (2K16→25, TTWO), shipping 2015→2024; real US street dates + cover athletes from Wikipedia / publisher press releases |
| Events resolvable | all **20** of 20 launches have publisher+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (publisher − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); a Newey-West (HAC) *t* on the date-ordered series as a robustness cross-check; Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; per-publisher and sub-era splits; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; drift = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported. Execution lag = 0 (the launch date is calendar-known years ahead) |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for all three legs |

**Survivorship (named on the Signal axis):** EA and TTWO are both **survivors** — large,
still-listed publishers — so there is no delisting bias in the panel, but by the same
token the sample cannot speak to a franchise/publisher that failed. **Attribution caveat:**
a single annual sports title is a small slice of a multi-franchise publisher's revenue
(EA also ships FC/Apex; TTWO also ships GTA/Rockstar), so any launch signal competes with
a lot of unrelated news — a structural reason to expect nothing.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the launch (publisher − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | *t* (Newey-West) | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week run-up (k=5) | 20 | +0.048% | +0.072 | +0.090 | 10/20 = 50.0% [29.9%, 70.1%] |
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 20 | −0.168% | −0.197 | −0.227 | 10/20 = 50.0% [29.9%, 70.1%] |

The "buy the hype" run-up is a **clean zero**: the publisher does not rally into the
launch (both cuts |*t*| < 0.25, hit rate an exact coin-flip 10/20). There is no
anticipation premium to ride.

## The launch drift — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the launch

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | *t* (Newey-West) | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week drift (k=5) | 20 | −1.213% | −1.889 | −1.556 | 8/20 = 40.0% [21.9%, 61.3%] |
| 2-week drift (k=10) | 20 | −0.781% | −0.906 | −1.084 | 9/20 = 45.0% [25.8%, 65.8%] |

If anything the publisher **drifts down** after the launch — a mild "sell the news" lean
(−1.21% in the first week). But it is **not significant** (one-sample *t* = −1.89, |*t*| <
2; the HAC *t* is milder still at −1.56) and it is the **wrong sign for "buy the hype":**
a curse-buyer going long the publisher into the launch would have *lost* to SPY, not won.
It is a faint post-ship dip indistinguishable from noise, not an edge.

## Per-publisher & sub-era robustness — 2-week launch drift

| split | n | mean AR | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| EA (Madden) | 10 | −0.247% | −0.242 |
| TTWO (NBA 2K) | 10 | −1.315% | −0.923 |
| Early era 2015–2019 | 10 | −0.029% | −0.042 |
| Late era 2020–2024 | 10 | −1.532% | −0.966 |

The faint dip does **not** hold up robustly: EA's is essentially zero, only TTWO leans
(insignificantly) negative, and the early era is a flat zero while the late era carries
what little lean there is — the opposite of a stable, era-spanning effect. Nothing clears
|*t*| ≥ 2 in any slice.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −0.168% | +0.285% (1.191%) | 0.645 |
| 2-week drift | right | −0.781% | +0.285% (1.191%) | 0.823 |

Both observed means sit **deep inside** the luck cloud of ordinary random 2-week windows
(right-tail p = 0.65 and 0.82). The pre- and post-launch moves are exactly what these two
stocks' tracking noise produces on any random fortnight — no special launch effect.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week launch drift *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.906**; across all 20 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.355, −0.369]** — so no single launch drives the (already insignificant) dip, and it
never comes anywhere near |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Tradability — net of costs

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −0.168% (*t* −0.20) | −0.268% (*t* −0.31) | −0.368% (*t* −0.43) |
| 2-week drift | −0.781% (*t* −0.91) | −0.881% (*t* −1.02) | −0.981% (*t* −1.14) |

There is no significant edge to bank gross, and costs only deepen the (insignificant)
negative windows. "Buy the hype" is a *losing* long here; the mirror "sell the news" short
is not significant either, and shorting a large-cap publisher for a two-week fade around a
telegraphed annual ship is not a business.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (drift = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.34 (sd 0.99); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds —
  the small-sample false-positive rate at n = 20 events with a 10-day AR is honest (~5%),
  so the detector does not manufacture significance on the null.
- **Planted launch drift +2.0% (seed 844):** mean AR moves +2.00% vs the null, *t* = +0.49.
- **Planted launch drift +4.0% (seed 844):** mean AR moves +4.00% vs the null, *t* = **+2.06** —
  the planted drift is recovered with unit slope (each +1% planted → +1% measured), and a
  large-enough bump clears significance. The machinery works; the real tape simply has no
  bump to find (and what lean it has points the wrong way for the claim).

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | The "buy the hype" run-up is a clean zero (2-week +0.05% / −0.17%, \|*t*\| < 0.25, hit 10/20). The post-launch move, if anything, drifts *down* (1-week −1.21%) — but it is **not significant** (*t* = −1.89, HAC *t* = −1.56, \|*t*\| < 2), it is the **wrong sign** for a "buy the publisher" claim, it sits deep inside the placebo cloud (right-tail p = 0.82), and it does not survive per-publisher (EA *t* = −0.24) or sub-era (early *t* = −0.04) splits. The synthetic control shows a real bump *would* have been caught. Indistinguishable from noise. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank: no significant edge gross or net, "buy the hype" is a losing long, the mirror short is insignificant, and a two-week fade trade around a telegraphed annual ship on a large-cap publisher is not a business. |

**In one sentence:** the finance version of the "Madden curse" is a bust — across 20
*Madden* and *NBA 2K* launches (2015→2024) EA and TTWO neither reliably rally into the ship
date (a clean zero) nor pop after it (a faint, insignificant *dip* if anything, the wrong
way for "buy the hype"), and every faint lean drowns in ordinary tracking noise.
